questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Software timers and callback rules”?
options: Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
A software timer is not a precise hardware timer; measure jitter and scheduler load.
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
questions.answer: A software timer is not a precise hardware timer; measure jitter and scheduler load.
questions.explanation:
A software timer is not a precise hardware timer; measure jitter and scheduler load.
Why: A software timer callback runs in the timer-service task. Keep it short: blocking, lengthy Serial output, or expensive sensor work can delay every software timer. Send longer work to a worker task through a queue or notification.
